title: Compare two states, not a compression movie
question: What is held fixed when volume changes?
recap: For the same energy and narrow frequency band, Wien radiation gains entropy logarithmically with accessible volume. Both endpoint states must remain in the admitted regime.
premises: Energy E, central frequency ν, and bandwidth Δν are fixed in both states.
The entropy-density constant has been fixed by the zero-radiation condition.
Both states satisfy the dilute Wien-regime and narrow-band assumptions.
limitations: A moving mirror generally changes frequency and energy, so it is not this held-fixed comparison.
The result is not valid merely because one of the two endpoint states is dilute.

overview.text: For the same energy and narrow frequency band, Wien radiation gains entropy logarithmically with accessible volume. Both endpoint states must remain in the admitted regime.

full.text: Within a narrow band, write E = V Δν ρν and S = V Δν sν. Substitute ρν = E/(V Δν) into the integrated entropy density. Comparing V with V₀ at the same E and band removes terms independent of volume.

full.spoken: The entropy difference is E over B frequency times the natural logarithm of the volume ratio.

full.text: E/(Bν) has entropy units. Only after identifying B = h/k_B can it be written k_B times the dimensionless coefficient E/(hν). This distinction matters when interpreting a displayed coefficient as a count.

full.spoken: An unfixed entropy-density constant would add bandwidth times C of frequency times the volume difference.

full.text: Doubling the accessible volume adds (E/(Bν)) ln 2 under the stated constraints. Doubling it again adds the same amount. The radiation-entropy laboratory compares those constrained states and exposes the otherwise hidden constant.

full.returnCaption: Return to keeping energy and the narrow band fixed.

items: Write the energy density in the initial state as E/(V₀ Δν).
Write the energy density in the final state as E/(V Δν).
Check the approximation at both densities before comparing them.
Multiply each spectral entropy density by its own V Δν to obtain total entropy.
Subtract the two total entropies; the logarithms leave ln(V/V₀).
Retaining C(ν) would leave Δν C(ν)(V − V₀), so fixing it was essential.
Do not replace this state comparison with an adiabatic moving-wall trajectory.

margin.text: A modern pointwise comparison gives relative spectral-density error exp(−hν/(k_B T)) for Wien versus Planck. That diagnostic is not, by itself, an error bound for the entire integrated entropy argument.
